questions.q: What are the Redshift Serverless workgroup and namespace names for this warehouse?
options: Workgroup northfield-analytics, namespace northfield-dw
There is no named workgroup; it uses the AWS account default
Workgroup northfield-redshift, namespace northfield-orders
Workgroup northfield-dw, namespace northfield-analytics
questions.explain: The workgroup is northfield-analytics, backed by namespace northfield-dw, database northfielddw, at base capacity 8 RPUs.

questions.q: Why is region left as a column on fact_orders instead of becoming a fourth dimension table?
options: It's a flat attribute of the order with no further descriptive detail worth normalizing out
Redshift does not allow more than three dimension tables per fact table
It was a mistake that gets corrected in a later lesson
Region values change too often to store in a dimension table
questions.explain: region has no additional attributes to normalize into its own table, so it stays directly on the fact table rather than becoming an unnecessary fourth dimension.

questions.q: What does DISTKEY(customer_id) on fact_orders accomplish?
options: It prevents duplicate customer_id values from ever being loaded
It sorts the table alphabetically by customer name
It colocates each customer's fact rows with that customer's dim_customer row on the same compute slice, speeding up that join
It encrypts the customer_id column at rest
questions.explain: DISTKEY(customer_id) means matching rows for a given customer land on the same slice, letting the join to dim_customer happen locally instead of shuffling data across the cluster.

questions.q: Why does SORTKEY(dt) help the kind of queries Finance and Ops actually run?
options: It makes every column in the table load faster, regardless of what's filtered
Rows are physically ordered by date, so a date-range filter can skip blocks outside that range entirely
It automatically deletes old partitions outside the sort range
It has no real performance effect and is purely cosmetic
questions.explain: With rows physically ordered by dt, a filter like 'last month' or 'last 7 days' only has to scan the overlapping blocks, skipping the rest of the table's history.

questions.q: Why is Redshift Serverless (rather than an always-on provisioned cluster) the right fit here?
options: An always-on cluster would actually cost less for this exact workload
Provisioned clusters cannot run joins across multiple tables
Northfield's query load is bursty around month-end, and Serverless auto-pauses and bills per RPU-second
Serverless is the only Redshift option that supports SORTKEY
questions.explain: Serverless's auto-pause and per-RPU-second billing fits a workload that spikes at month-end and is quiet otherwise, far better than paying for always-on capacity sized for the busiest day.
